question: Should a contract version difference block a client?
rationale: Clients are refused whenever prod and client differ by a contract version, even when only a block was added: a newer TUI could not connect while a prod deploy waited, and the Mac app cannot update itself yet. With simple blocks (D-0104) clients can show unknown content plainly instead of failing.

options.text: Tolerant clients; a version difference is a warning
options.details: Unknown blocks render plainly, properties optional, additive contract changes, answers still checked by Control.
options.rule: Clients are tolerant readers and a contract version never blocks a client. A client skips unknown markup, treats every block property as optional, and renders an unknown block with a plain fallback (its title and text), so it always shows some information and never fails. Control and the contract change only additively: new block types and fields may be added; an existing block or field never changes meaning (a changed meaning is a new block or field, the old one retired later). Client and Control tell each other their versions; a difference is shown as a status warning, not a refusal. Answers stay strict on Control's side: a client may only send answers Control offered on that page, and Control checks each again.
options.consequences: Control's hello stops refusing other contract versions; the status line warns about a version difference (and the TUI still updates itself). TUI, Mac app and agent CLI get fallback rendering for unknown blocks and optional properties. Contract reviews check that changes are additive. The Mac app keeps working on a newer prod even while it cannot update itself.

options.text: Keep the contract version as a gate
options.details: Control refuses clients that speak another contract version.
